claims.text: Multiphase BCC-based high-entropy alloys with VEC values between 4.4 and 6.87 will exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
The non-monotonic ductility transition is driven by a sequence of order-disorder transformations followed by coherent precipitation.
Initial chemical ordering induces brittleness.
Later formation of coherent, strain-relieving nanoprecipitates restores ductility.
The starting material is a supersaturated, chemically homogeneous BCC-based HEA solid solution.
Arc melting under argon can produce chemically homogeneous Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-family ingots.
Aging between 600 and 1000 °C under argon, including a 15-hour duration, is applicable to Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-family alloys.
Multistage thermomechanical processing can produce stepwise, independently controllable coherent nanoprecipitation.
Mechanical properties can be assessed at ambient temperature and at temperatures up to 800 °C.
Aging first produces short-range order or ordered B2/L2_1-type phases.
Short-range or long-range chemical ordering increases lattice distortion and slip resistance.
Coherent Ni3Ta-based delta and gamma-double-prime precipitates can be generated through stepwise processing.
Negative enthalpy of mixing drives initial chemical ordering.
The ordered lattice becomes rigid and brittle because it impedes dislocation motion.
Coherent precipitates accommodate lattice strain and favor dislocation looping or shearing over cleavage.
Traditional high-damping alloys exhibit an inverse relationship between mobile-defect-mediated damping and strength or ductility.
Controlled coherent precipitation breaks the inverse scaling between damping and strength or ductility.
Uniform tensile elongation will follow a U-shaped aging-time dependence, with high initial ductility, an intermediate minimum, and recovery at long times.
BCC solid solutions are generally favored below a VEC of 6.87, while the proposed transition specifically occurs for 4.4 < VEC < 6.87.
The transition fails above the coherent-precipitate solvus or when topologically close-packed phases such as the mu phase form and cause irreversible embrittlement.

contradictions.description: The proposed Ni3Ta-based delta precipitate cannot form in the explicitly named AlCoCrFeNi example, which contains no Ta, or in the explicitly named W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V example, which contains no Ni, unless additional compositional modifications are introduced.
